chapter: Arrival and the Pete Lala photograph
title: Identifying the musicians in the Pete Lala cabaret photograph
summary: They name Valtuli, Buddy Christian, Frankie Keeling, Henry Zeno and Bill Packer in the photo; Clarence Williams is recalled getting a job in 1916.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: He ought to know. I don't know if you recognize them.
Yes, you can tell the students in that.
I can't see so good. I know them. I know some of them.

Valtuli on the violin. That's Buddy Christian, guitar. Buddy Christian, guitar. And that's Frankie Keeling. Frankie Keeling. And that's Zeno. Henry Zeno is the drummer. Henry Zeno. And I think that's Packer. What's his name? Bass player. Bill Packer. Wasn't he a bass player? Bill Packer. Who's the drum man? Bill Packer's the drum player. Who's that bass player, Papa? Ike. Ike something. Ike Jackson. Was that Ike Jackson? Playing with your Pete? Yeah. Was it Ike Jackson? Mm-hmm.
Well, that's the one it must have been. I didn't know him. I didn't know the other fellas. I didn't know everybody else. I know his little... Is your father in there? Yeah, he's on there.
My daddy's there. He's on there now.
I can see him. Is Valtuli? Valtuli the violin. Buddy Christian on the guitar. He was a piano player at the cabaret, you see? And he also played a little guitar.
Yes, I knew him in New York. Played with Clarence Williams. Frank Keeling on.
Huh? Yes, Frank Keeling. Yeah, that's a fine place.
You remember Clarence Williams, mister? I said, you remember Clarence Williams? I knew Clarence Williams in New York, yes. And that's Zeno on drums. I've never seen him.
Clarence Williams got the job in 1916. Clarence Williams got me my job in 1916. I gave him $100.
I wish you could find a picture of the craftsman band.
And that's Valtuli on violin. I've never seen his picture. And Keeling. And Valtuli is a very nice looking man. Yes, he is.
